div.div:
Failure Event (AZ-A goes down):
Restore latest snapshot as a new volume in AZ-B.
Update nodeSelector in StatefulSet to AZ-B.
Pod restarts in AZ-B and attaches to the new volume

div.div:
If your database writes a large 1 MB (1024 KiB) chunk of data:
You might think: "That’s 1 operation."
But AWS says: "That’s 1024 / 256 = 4 IOPS.

div.div: Why it matters: If you have a 3,000 IOPS limit and you do a lot of large sequential writes, you will "run out" of IOPS much faster than you expect.

Baseline: gp3 gives a flat 3,000 IOPS free, with no burst credits

div.div: If load stays high for hours, the gp2 "fuel tank" empties and AWS caps you at baseline (3 IOPS/GiB). gp3 has no tank: provision IOPS explicitly.
